subject: measurement invariance test with function measurementInvariance()

messages.author: cc3e8d7d11a99465
messages.subject: measurement invariance test with function measurementInvariance()
parts:
Hello,

I am testing measurement invariance of a few constructs.
The problem is that I did it in two ways and the solution (p value) does not correspond when I use the function measurementInvariance()

Syntax 1 (when I do the steps myself without the function)
fitRisk <- sem(myModelRisk, data=myData, se = "robust", test="Satorra-Bentler",group="Code_country")
#Step 2: full metric invariance (constrain the factor loadings)
fitRisk2 <- sem(myModelRisk, data=myData, se = "robust", test="Satorra-Bentler",group="Code_country",group.equal="loadings")
summary(fitRisk2, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)
anova(fitRisk,fitRisk2)
#Step3: partial metric invariance
fitRisk3 <- sem(myModelRisk, data=myData, se = "robust", test="Satorra-Bentler",group="Code_country",group.equal="loadings",group.partial=c("construct_risk_perc =~ q9_5","construct_risk_perc =~ q9_4", "construct_risk_perc =~ q9_3"))
summary(fitRisk3, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)
anova(fitRisk,fitRisk3)

Output Syntax 1
> anova(fitRisk,fitRisk3)
Scaled Chi Square Difference Test (test = satorra.bentler)
         Df   AIC   BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fitRisk  70 57703 58331 2215.6                             
fitRisk3 82 57697 58253 2233.8     16.993      12     0.1499


Syntax 2:When I use the function measurementInvariance() and group.partial (like I did in Step3 of Syntax 1)
measurementInvariance(myModelRisk, data = myData, group = "Code_country",group.partial=c("construct_risk_perc =~ q9_5","construct_risk_perc =~ q9_4","construct_risk_perc =~ q9_3"))

Output Syntax 2

Measurement invariance tests:

Model 1: configural invariance:
    chisq        df    pvalue       cfi     rmsea       bic
 2215.627    70.000     0.000     0.907     0.229 58330.548

Model 2: weak invariance (equal loadings):
    chisq        df    pvalue       cfi     rmsea       bic
 2233.763    82.000     0.000     0.907     0.212 58252.944

[Model 1 versus model 2]
  delta.chisq      delta.df delta.p.value     delta.cfi
       18.136        12.000         0.112         0.000

Problem: Syntax 2 gives me another p value than syntax 1?

What is the explanation for this? Or did I something wrong?

Thank you in advance!
Kind regards,
Silke

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance test with function measurementInvariance()
parts:
Hi Silke,

In your code you used the Satorra-Bentler chi-square, whereas with the measurement invariance function you're the plain, vanilla, ML chi-square. You can add test="Satorra-Bentler" to the measurement invariance function and things should look the same.

Alex
